extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, motor carriers, drivers, industry stakeholders, and advocacy groups submitting comments to FMCSA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments in response to FMCSA notices of proposed rulemaking (NPRMs), including preferred submission channels, content expectations, and evidence that strengthens comments. Aimed at stakeholders who want their comments considered in FMCSA rulemaking dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted via: Federal eRulemaking Portal (http://www.regulations.gov, identified by the docket number), Mail (Docket Operations, U.S. Department of Transportation), Hand Delivery (address provided), or Fax (1-202-493-2251).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the method most convenient, but ensure you identify the correct docket number when submitting. Physical delivery address and fax number are provided for alternatives to online submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission channel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations.gov is the preferred method; it associates submissions directly with the docket and makes them publicly viewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the specific docket number
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference the specific docket number in the body of your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the docket number in the comment text helps ensure your submission is associated with the correct rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the questions FMCSA poses in the NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the questions FMCSA poses in the NPRM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly responding to the agency's specific questions increases the usefulness and relevance of your comment to the agency's decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include data on safety impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative or qualitative evidence demonstrating how the proposed action or alternatives would affect driver or public safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include motor carrier cost information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include data on motor carrier costs (cost-of-compliance estimates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed, supportable cost estimates showing how compliance would affect motor carriers (e.g., small and large carriers), including assumptions and calculations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include driver impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the proposal would affect drivers (work conditions, hours, safety, fatigue) with supporting evidence where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific FMCSA regulations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing applicable regulatory citations helps situate your comment within the existing regulatory framework and clarifies which provisions you are discussing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain technical operational impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe operational or technical effects (e.g., how equipment, procedures, or business operations would change) and provide concrete examples or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide driver safety data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply verifiable safety metrics, crash reduction estimates, or other empirical measures that demonstrate safety outcomes relevant to the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide crash statistics with verifiable sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reliable, citable sources for crash data and document the data's provenance so FMCSA can verify and use it in the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide hours-of-service / fatigue research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit peer-reviewed studies, government reports, or well-documented analyses relating to hours-of-service and driver fatigue to support claims about safety or operational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide technology integration considerations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how electronic logging devices, automatic onboard recording devices, or other technologies would interact with the proposed rule, including implementation challenges and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide inspection and audit experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share firsthand inspection or audit observations that bear on practicability, compliance issues, enforcement, or safety implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer small motor carrier perspectives (RFA implications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe impacts on small entities and provide information useful for Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) analysis, such as burdens or disproportionate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments are publicly available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware submissions become part of the public docket; do not include information you do not want public unless you follow the agency's process for submitting confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit confidential business information except as marked
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit confidential business information except as marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you must provide confidential business information (CBI), follow FMCSA's instructions for submitting such material so it can be properly protected; otherwise assume comments will be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Late comments may not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments within the docket's stated comment period to ensure they are considered in the rulemaking; late submissions risk exclusion from the administrative record.
